- **Animal-powered machines (horse gin, treadwheel)** [`animal_power_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/animal_power_gin.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Donkeys and slaves turn hourglass-shaped lava mills in the bakeries; men tread wheels for cranes and drainage. Horses pull poorly in the throat-and-girth harness. Local: bakeries (pistrina) with donkey mills (mola asinaria, already in Cato).
- **Water wheel** [`water_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_wheel.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Rivers turning wheels with scoops are a familiar sight (Lucretius, book 5). A grain mill stood at Mithridates' palace; none is attested at Rome. Bakers have donkeys and slaves. Local: Tiber and Anio; Vitruvius, who will describe the geared mill in the 20s BC. Elsewhere: Cabeira in Pontus: water mill at Mithridates' palace, in Roman hands since the 60s BC (Strabo).
- **Windmill** [`windmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Unknown anywhere. Sailcloth, carpenters and right-angle gearing exist. Winds at Rome are weak and fickle; coasts and hilltops suit better.
- **Water turbine** [`water_turbine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_turbine.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Crank, connecting rod and flywheel** [`crank_connecting_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crank_connecting_rod.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The rotary hand quern has an upright handle at its rim, a crank in all but name. Crank with connecting rod and flywheel is built nowhere. Local: hand querns in every legionary tent group.
- **Piston pumps (suction and force pump)** [`piston_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/piston_pump.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Ctesibius' twin-cylinder bronze force pump is described in Greek mechanics; founders and turners here could build one. Rome has no fire brigade, only buckets and private slave gangs. Local: bronze founders and turners; the fire-prone tenements (insulae) of the Subura. Elsewhere: Alexandria: Ctesibius' pumps and water organ (3rd c. BC).
- **Hydraulic ram** [`hydraulic_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_ram.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Lead pipe and bronze valves are at hand, but pipes are folded sheet with a soldered seam and burst under water hammer. Hillside villas would want it.
- **Charcoal burning** [`charcoal_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charcoal_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Charcoal feeds smiths, founders and house braziers; wood and charcoal come down the Tiber from Apennine forests. Nobody collects the tar and vinegar from the smoke.
- **Deep coal mining (drainage, ventilation, safety lamp)** [`coal_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coal_mining.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Theophrastus (On Stones) reports earthy coals burnt by smiths in Liguria and Elis. Central Italy has no good seams; those of Gaul and Britain lie unworked. Elsewhere: Han China: coal burnt as fuel.

- **Argand lamp (hollow wick and glass chimney)** [`argand_lamp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/argand_lamp.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Olive-oil lamps of clay and bronze with a solid wick light every house. A tubular wick and bronze burner are possible; a thin glass chimney is not.
- **Drilling for brine, gas and oil** [`oil_drilling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oil_drilling.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Bitumen and naphtha from natural seeps are known and traded as caulk, drug and curiosity. Wells are dug, never drilled. Elsewhere: Han China, Sichuan: percussion-drilled brine wells.
- **Steam reaction toy (aeolipile)** [`steam_aeolipile`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steam_aeolipile.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Bronze balls that blow steam from a pinhole are a curiosity used to explain wind; Vitruvius names them about 25 BC. A spinning version is easy, a toy.
- **Boilers and the safety valve** [`safety_valve_boiler`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/safety_valve_boiler.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Bath boilers are open bronze cauldrons over a furnace. Riveted or soft-soldered sheet holds little pressure; brazed seams and a weighted valve must be taught. Local: bath furnaces and hypocausts (Sergius Orata's raised-floor 'hanging' baths, before 91 BC).
